element: ReproRepo (Li et al. 2026, Scaling Reproducibility Audits with GitHub Repository Issues)

UC1.note: No artifact appendix or venue-format document is produced; output is a findings.json list of predicted reproduction blockers.

UC3.evidence: "evidence": [{"path": "...", "line_refs": "...", ...}], ... "affected_claims_or_metrics": ["..."] (Sec. E.1 agent prompt, findings.json schema, p.17)
UC3.note: Current 0 is debatable: each finding must cite repo file paths/line refs and the paper claims or metrics it affects, i.e. claim-to-artifact links, but only for problematic items, not a full claim map.

UC4.evidence: missing or ambiguous data/checkpoint/model artifacts - broken or incomplete installation/dependency instructions - missing scripts/configs/paths referenced by the paper or README (Sec. E.1 agent prompt, p.16)
UC4.note: Reports missing files, deps and instructions as a deliverable, but relative to the paper/README and general reproducibility expectations, not an explicit venue standard S; partial is right.

UC5.evidence: Silent wrong setup: the released setup does not match the paper's intended configuration, artifact scope, checkpoint, data provenance, or evaluation path (Sec. B.2, p.12); finding category paper_repo_mismatch (Sec. E.1, p.17)
UC5.note: Current 0 is wrong: the agent is explicitly asked to surface paper/repository mismatches and result/metric provenance gaps, which the rubric says counts as at least partial.

UC6.note: The agent is forbidden to run or generate anything: 'Write exactly one required artifact: ./findings.json' (Sec. E.1, p.17).

UC7.note: Comparison is against hidden human GitHub issues for the same repo, not against exemplar (P,A) pairs from the domain.

B1.evidence: The property is practically useful for reviewer or author triage when humans only have limited bandwidth to check a few potential issues. (Sec. 5.2, p.8)
B1.note: Paper names reviewers and authors together ('reviewer-facing budget', Sec. 3.3), and the framework itself targets benchmark builders; 3 would also be defensible, but the audit is a third-party inspection of a released repo, so 4 stands.

B2.evidence: The agent is instructed to perform a static inspection without environment setup and code execution. GPU compute is withheld from the workspace. (Sec. 3.2, p.4)
B2.note: The agent does read source code, configs and dependency files (not only docs), but never executes; 1 is correct on this scale, 2 at most.

B3.evidence: Adding the paper improves performance across all metrics ... repository inspection alone can often identify the broad failure region, as reflected by the strong code-only semantic match rates (Sec. 5.2, p.8)
B3.note: Current 3 is debatable: inputs are paper+repo, but findings are grounded in repository evidence (path, line_refs) and the code-only ablation retains 87.6% vs 89.7% SM@10, so the repo is the primary input.

B4.evidence: Our key idea is to use real reproduction pain as supervision: instead of relying on experts to manually design tasks, inject errors, or write evaluation rubrics, ReproRepo leverages GitHub issues (Sec. 1, p.1)
B4.note: No venue standard or published checklist drives the audit; only an ad hoc list of finding categories in the prompt.

B5.evidence: "issue_title": "...", "user_symptom": "...", "trigger_context": "...", "root_cause": "...", ... "impact": "..." (Sec. E.1 findings.json schema, p.17); main metrics are EM rate and SM rate (Sec. 3.3, p.4)
B5.note: Current 2 is debatable: the framework emits match-rate scores, but the audit agent's deliverable is a ranked JSON report of prose findings with severity/category labels, i.e. a structured report, so 3 is a fairer midpoint.

disagreements: UC5: current 0, should be 1 because the agent is explicitly prompted to report 'paper/repository mismatches' and 'result/metric provenance gaps' (Sec. E.1, p.16) with a paper_repo_mismatch category, and 'silent wrong setup' is defined as released setup not matching the paper's intended configuration (Sec. B.2, p.12); rubric says paper-artifact inconsistency detection counts as at least partial.

UC3: current 0, arguably 1 because every finding must carry repo evidence (path, line_refs) plus affected_claims_or_metrics (Sec. E.1, p.17), which are explicit claim-to-artifact links, though only for blockers rather than a full claim map (medium confidence).

B3: current 3, arguably 4 because findings are grounded in repository file evidence and the code-only ablation keeps most performance (87.6% vs 89.7% paper-level SM@10, Table 6, p.8); the paper is a secondary input that sharpens exact matching (medium confidence).

B5: current 2, arguably 3 because the agent's deliverable is a ranked findings.json of prose fields (symptom, trigger, root cause, impact) with severity/category labels, while only the framework layer emits match-rate scores (medium confidence).
one_line_summary: Benchmark framework: LLM agents statically audit paper+repo snapshots (no execution) to predict GitHub-issue-style reproduction blockers, scored by LLM-judge match against hidden human-reported issues.
